svg.title: Prompting techniques: demonstrations and persona are separate choices
svg.desc: Panel A compares three prompts for the same customer message about a missing package. The categories are Billing, Delivery, and Login. Zero-shot gives no examples. One-shot shows a package sent to the wrong address, categorized as Delivery. Few-shot adds a double charge for Billing and a sign-in problem for Login. The expected category is Delivery. Panel B asks two team leads to choose a single change for smaller mobile API responses and give a trade-off. The mobile team lead is measured on how quickly the team ships mobile changes and may favor a mobile-only API. The platform team lead is measured on keeping the number of services low and may favor updating the shared API. Both receive the same task.

text.tspan: Examples and roles change different parts of a prompt
Two comparisons. Change one ingredient at a time.
A
Compare the number of worked examples
Keep the same customer message, category choices, and response format.
Customer message
My package hasn't arrived.
Choose one category: Billing, Delivery, or Login. Reply with the category only.
Prompt variant
Worked examples before the new message
Zero-shot
0 examples
No examples.
One-shot
1 example
My package arrived at the wrong address. → Delivery
Few-shot
3 examples
My package arrived at the wrong address. → Delivery
I was charged twice. → Billing
I can't sign in. → Login
Expected category: Delivery.
B
Give two team leads the same decision
ShopEasy's mobile app needs smaller responses. The team can fund one change this sprint.
Build a mobile-only API (a BFF) or add smaller responses to the shared API.
Choose one option and give one trade-off in two short sentences.
Mobile team lead
You lead the mobile team. Your team is
measured on how quickly it can ship mobile
changes.
May favor a mobile-only API.
Platform team lead
You lead the platform team. Your team is
measured on keeping the number of services
it runs low.
May favor updating the shared API.
Both leads get the same task. Their incentives pull in different directions.
Compare the options they choose and the trade-offs they point out.
Zero-shot still has instructions. Shots count worked input → output demonstrations, not requests.
